questions.question_text_en: Among the following one is a major feature of autocratic governments. Which one?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Exercising unlimited power

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Protection of human rights and freedom

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The absence of written constitution

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The prevalence of the rule of law

explanation.solution_text_en: Autocratic government concentrates political power in a ruler or small group with weak effective limits. Exercising unlimited or arbitrary power therefore best fits the defining feature among the options.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Democracy and Democratization; Unit 3: Good Governance

questions.question_text_en: The tendency to promote an ethnocentric point of view affects cultural equality and weakens the unity of a country, if it
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: fails to consider the cultural and religious practices of others

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: views any particular sets of customs, norms and values as relative

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: creates a common economic and political space

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: promotes the common interest that is in conflict with the personal

explanation.solution_text_en: Ethnocentrism judges other groups through the standards of one's own group and can treat other cultures as inferior. Failing to respect other cultural and religious practices therefore weakens equality and unity in diversity.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Units 5-6: Multiculturalism; National Unity through Diversity

questions.question_text_en: How the federal principle in Ethiopia devolves power between the regional state and the federal?
questions.review_note: The constitutional arrangement is more accurately described as a division/allocation of powers by the Constitution, not a discretionary grant from the federal government. B is the closest available option.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: There exists nominal devolution of power not the actual one

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: The federal government has devolved power to the regional states

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Regional states and the federal government have no properly defined power sharing schemes

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The federal principle exists on paper not reality in the world

explanation.solution_text_en: Ethiopia's federal system constitutionally allocates powers between the federal government and the states. Among the options, B is the closest to this division/devolution of authority to regional states. Evidence check: FDRE Constitution, Arts. 50-52 - federal/state structure and powers (Refworld).
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 5: Federalism in Ethiopia; FDRE Constitution Arts. 50-52

questions.question_text_en: The basic necessity behind the promulgation and compliance of tax law is
questions.review_note: Tax law also serves revenue collection, fairness, compliance and administration. B is the broadest development-oriented answer, but the stem is wider than a single objective.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: monitoring the fair collection of tax to maintain income equality

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: alleviating poverty and bringing inclusive development

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: to control the private sector from tax evasion and fraud

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: assisting government projects to become planned and executed

explanation.solution_text_en: Taxation finances public services and can support redistribution, poverty reduction and inclusive development. The current economics curriculum treats revenue, equity and development as important objectives of taxation.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 Economics - Unit 5: Tax Theory and Practice; Unit 6: Poverty and Inequality

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is among the qualities of patriotic citizens?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Promoting the public interest at local and national levels

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Inconsistent to implement government policies and strategies

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Helping the government in its good and bad work

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Criticizing blindly the government policies and strategies

explanation.solution_text_en: Patriotism includes commitment to the common good and constructive contribution to society. Promoting public interest at local and national levels fits this civic quality better than blind support or blind criticism.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Patriotism

questions.question_text_en: Mr.X is a well-respected man living in a small town of Y Regional State. Though he is well known and respected, he usually beats his wife at home. Mr.X, Mrs.Z's wife, sued her husband for beating her badly. The first court that sees Mrs. Z's case is
questions.review_note: The Constitution establishes federal and state judicial systems, but the exact first-instance jurisdiction of a domestic-violence case depends on applicable state law and procedure. B is the intended answer among the options.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Federal Higher Court

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: State First Instance Court

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Federal First Instance Court

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: State Supreme Court

explanation.solution_text_en: A dispute arising under ordinary state jurisdiction normally begins within the state court structure; among the listed courts, the State First Instance Court is the intended entry-level forum. Evidence check: FDRE Constitution, Art. 78 - federal and state judicial systems (Refworld).
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 5: Federalism in Ethiopia; FDRE Constitution Art. 78

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following describes the ways through which common good could be promoted?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Promoting one's own personal interest prior to others

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Failing to appreciate and tolerate differences

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Discouraging chauvinism and safeguarding our sovereignty

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Favoring and disfavoring individuals and groups subjectively

explanation.solution_text_en: The common good is promoted by conduct that protects shared interests and respects others. Discouraging chauvinism and safeguarding sovereignty supports social cohesion and national welfare.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 6: National Unity through Diversity; Grade 10 - Unit 7: Patriotism

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following alternatives states the quality of a patriotic citizen?
questions.review_note: Protection of military information must be lawful and compatible with rights such as freedom of expression; it is not a blanket justification for censorship.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: A journalist who keeps the secret of the national defense and military strategy

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: A chauvinist who thinks that his/her nation is superior to others

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: A nationalist who uses different tactics to achieve his/her political goals

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: A freedom fighter who destroys public property and civilian lives

explanation.solution_text_en: A patriotic citizen may have a duty to protect legitimate national-security information entrusted to him or her. The other choices involve chauvinism, harmful political tactics, or destruction of civilian life/property.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Patriotism; Grade 9 - Unit 8: Foreign Relations

questions.question_text_en: Among the following one is different from the rest in terms of responsibility. Which one?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Punctuality at work and elsewhere

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Respecting the norms and values of society

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Choosing a way of life that could help one to be successful

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Honesty and keeping a promise

explanation.solution_text_en: Punctuality, respecting social norms, honesty and keeping promises are commonly framed as duties or ethical responsibilities toward others. Choosing a personal lifestyle for one's own success is primarily a personal choice, so it differs from the rest.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Ethical Values

questions.question_text_en: A responsibility that involves respecting the constitution, fighting the aggression of invaders, and resolving conflicts is
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Social Responsibility

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: National Responsibility

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Personal Responsibility

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Organizational Responsibility

explanation.solution_text_en: Respecting the constitution, defending the country from aggression and contributing to conflict resolution are duties connected with the security and welfare of the nation.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Patriotism; Unit 4: Peace and Conflict Resolution

questions.question_text_en: Ato Bekele has given some amount of money for a human resource director of a certain construction company to let his son who graduated from a university be selected as a candidate for employment. The form of corruption which is committed in this way is
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: nepotism

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: abuse of power

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: embezzlement

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: bribery

explanation.solution_text_en: Offering money to influence an employment decision is bribery: giving an improper benefit to obtain favorable treatment. Nepotism would involve favoritism based on family relationship by the decision-maker.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 3: Good Governance

questions.question_text_en: One of the following cannot be classified as gender inequality in the case of contemporary Ethiopia?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The denial of women's right to vote

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Denial of equal access for women to land and other resources

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Women and girls suffering from harmful cultural practices

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Lack of encouragement of women in decision making

explanation.solution_text_en: The FDRE constitutional framework recognizes equal political participation and voting rights; denying women the right to vote is therefore not a lawful feature of contemporary Ethiopia. The other options describe recognized forms of gender inequality or harmful discrimination. Evidence check: FDRE Constitution, Arts. 35 and 38 - women's equality and electoral rights (Refworld).
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 6: Human Rights; FDRE Constitution Arts. 35 and 38

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following can be distinguished best as a struggle for justice?
questions.review_note: A, B and D also describe legitimate justice concerns. C is selected because it expresses the broadest general principle.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: A struggle for empowering women in development activities and poverty reduction

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: A struggle for a fair treatment of students with disability to those who are not

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: A struggle for the access of resources and opportunities without discrimination

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: A struggle to get equal payment with other citizens with similar ability

explanation.solution_text_en: Justice is broadly concerned with fair access to rights, resources and opportunities without discrimination. The other options are specific examples of justice, while C states the general principle most comprehensively.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 6: Human Rights; Unit 3: Good Governance

questions.question_text_en: In democratic countries, courts are legal institutions which are entrusted to
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: maintains the power of a certain political party

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: ensures a political order based on the interest of a single ethnic group

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: interprets the law and decides whether or not a person broke the law

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: protects the interest of the rulers

explanation.solution_text_en: Courts apply and interpret law in deciding disputes and determining whether conduct violates legal rules. Protecting a party, ruler or ethnic group is incompatible with judicial impartiality.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 3: Good Governance; Unit 6: Human Rights

questions.question_text_en: What was the main cause of an inefficient collection of taxes during the Socialist Derg regime?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: A disorder that is caused by the free market economy that has been set in place

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Monopoly of market system controlled by a single ethnic group

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: It collected most of the product from the farmers as taxes

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The suppression of private initiative and low production

explanation.solution_text_en: The Derg pursued socialist policies that nationalized major economic activities and restricted private initiative. Weak production and incentives can reduce the taxable base and make revenue collection less efficient.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 History - Unit 6: Ethiopia 1941-1991; Grade 12 Economics - Unit 7: Macroeconomic Reforms in Ethiopia

secondary_curriculum_links: Grade 12 Economics - Unit 7: Macroeconomic Reforms in Ethiopia

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following can be taken as a major cause for all types of corruption?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The personal interest of rulers

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: The weakness of religious institutions

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The breakdown of the rule of law

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The moral decadence of the society

explanation.solution_text_en: Corruption thrives where laws are not applied consistently and public power lacks effective accountability. Breakdown of rule of law is therefore the most systemic cause among the choices.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 3: Good Governance

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following clearly explains the concept of equality?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Equality is not about rights and benefits but also sharing burdens equally

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Equality may not imply that your guaranteed rights are guaranteed to others

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Equality refers to the provision of identical treatment and benefits

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Equality necessarily means an absolutely similar rights, benefits and opportunities

explanation.solution_text_en: Equality concerns fair enjoyment of rights and benefits together with fair sharing of duties and burdens. It does not always require identical treatment or identical outcomes in every circumstance.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 6: Human Rights

questions.question_text_en: Article 35 of the constitution of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia (FDRE) has recognized equality of women in that
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: women have more rights than men in marriage

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: laws, customs and practices that oppress women are prohibited

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: religious practices which discriminate women are prohibited

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: affirmative measures regarding women are prohibited

explanation.solution_text_en: Article 35 protects women's equality and states that laws, customs and practices that oppress or cause bodily or mental harm to women are prohibited. Evidence check: FDRE Constitution, Art. 35(4) - harmful laws, customs and practices against women prohibited (Refworld).
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 6: Human Rights; FDRE Constitution Art. 35

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following describes best the principle of equity of taxation?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: All activities which citizens do should be subjected to taxations

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Those who have less money should pay more taxes

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The government shall collect taxes equally from every citizen

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Those who have more money should pay more taxes

explanation.solution_text_en: Under the ability-to-pay principle of tax equity, taxpayers with greater economic capacity are expected to bear a greater tax burden. This is the idea of vertical equity.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 Economics - Unit 5: Tax Theory and Practice

questions.question_text_en: All activities that we do that are subjected to taxation are known as
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: business profit tax

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: tariffs and duties

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: tax rate

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: tax base

explanation.solution_text_en: The tax base is the income, property, transaction, activity or other amount on which a tax is imposed and calculated.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 Economics - Unit 5: Tax Theory and Practice

questions.question_text_en: All are factors which affect the selection of an appropriate economic system except
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: the ethno-linguistic composition of the country

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: the global economic trends which others are using

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: the economic potential of the country

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: the local man power and the climate condition

explanation.solution_text_en: Choice of an economic system is usually analyzed in relation to resources, productive capacity, institutions, development goals and the wider economic environment. Ethno-linguistic composition is not normally treated as a basic economic criterion for selecting an economic system.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 11 Economics - Economic Systems and Development; Grade 12 Economics - Macroeconomic Reforms

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following facts described as the impact of the Ethiopian student movement?
questions.review_note: The student movement also raised other major political questions, including the nationalities question. C is selected because the land question is the clearest option here.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The process of answering the religious question

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Establishing federal government

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The process of answering the land question

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The process of answering the ethnic equality question

explanation.solution_text_en: The Ethiopian student movement made the land question a central political issue, famously associated with the demand for land reform. This helped shape the political debate that preceded the 1974 Revolution. Evidence check: Current Grade 12 History, Unit 6 - Ethiopia 1941-1991 (MoE new curriculum textbook listing).
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 History - Unit 6: Ethiopia 1941-1991

questions.question_text_en: Self-reliance and decision making process are closely related in that;
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: self-reliant people do not feel inferior to others

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: a self-reliant person knows that he/she is capable of promoting the public interest

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: self-reliant people engage in constructive criticism and self-criticism

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: a self-reliant person has a good relationship with other people

explanation.solution_text_en: Self-reliance requires the capacity to assess one's own decisions and performance rather than depending on others. Constructive criticism and self-criticism support independent, evidence-based decision making.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Problem-Solving Skills; Unit 1: Ethical Values

questions.question_text_en: The quality of a self-reliant person that involves the process of evaluating one's own achievements and weaknesses in a fair way is
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: self-Criticism

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: dependability

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: open-mindedness

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: civility

explanation.solution_text_en: Self-criticism is the fair examination of one's own conduct, achievements and weaknesses so that future decisions can improve.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Problem-Solving Skills

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following describes the main feature of dependability?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: It is to be receptive to different ideas and arguments

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: It refers to those who always act to appease their friends and other people

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: It is a quality of oneself who always does what he says

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: It refers to a polite way of treating others

explanation.solution_text_en: Dependability means being reliable: doing what one has said or promised and being someone others can count on.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Ethical Values

questions.question_text_en: Among the following one can be classified as the role of civic societies in a democratic country. Which one?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Safeguarding the interest of the ruling party and controlling antigovernment resistance

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Serving the government in order to develop policies

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Creating the opportunity to coordinate antigovernment agents

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Creating access to information and lobbying to influence legislation

explanation.solution_text_en: Civil-society organizations can educate the public, provide information, represent interests and advocate or lobby for changes in laws and policy. These activities contribute to participation and accountability.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Democracy and Democratization; Unit 3: Good Governance

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is true concerning civic societies?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Institutions which have no role in the political independence of society

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Voluntary organizations run by the community regardless of the political system

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Institutions that are run by the government and serve the purpose of the government

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Community organizations determined by the political system

explanation.solution_text_en: Civil-society organizations are generally voluntary, non-state associations formed by citizens around shared interests or public purposes. They are not simply organs of government.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Democracy and Democratization

questions.question_text_en: One among the following choices is different from the others. Which one?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Environmental protection associations

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Professional associations

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Charity Organizations

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Political Parties

explanation.solution_text_en: Environmental, professional and charity associations are typical civil-society organizations. A political party is primarily organized to compete for and exercise political power, so it differs from the other three.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Democracy and Democratization

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is true concerning the relationship between information and decision making?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Reliability, right representation the amount of data and the analysis process are needed to make right decisions

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: In order to make right decisions, looking for the right source to ensure accuracy is the only criterion

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The nature and type of study cannot determine the amount of data needed

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Considering right representation and sample size necessarily lead to right decision

explanation.solution_text_en: Sound decisions require reliable information, an appropriate amount of data, representative evidence and proper analysis. No single factor alone guarantees a correct decision.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Problem-Solving Skills

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following can be classified as the definition of wisdom than knowledge?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: A mature understanding of things to make sensible decisions

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: An ability to determine alternative ways of doing things

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Skills that can be gained through education or experience

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Learning about particular facts, ideas or situations

explanation.solution_text_en: Wisdom is more than possession of facts; it is mature understanding and sound judgment used to make sensible decisions.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Problem-Solving Skills

questions.question_text_en: The skill to care and consider issues related to right and wrong decisions and actions is known as
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: self-assertiveness

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: independence

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: self-awareness

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: moral sensitivity

explanation.solution_text_en: Moral sensitivity is awareness of the ethical dimensions of a situation - recognizing how choices may be right or wrong and how they affect others.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Ethical Values

questions.question_text_en: All are major reasons behind the fact that the poor countries are getting poorer while the rich ones are getting richer except
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: debt and dependency

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: drought aid

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: international market

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: profit extraction

explanation.solution_text_en: Dependency perspectives often identify debt, unequal international markets and profit extraction as factors that can reproduce inequality between richer and poorer economies. Drought aid is emergency assistance, so it is the exception in this list.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 8: Globalization and Global Issues; Grade 11 Economics - Economic Development

questions.question_text_en: The non-consequential theory in that an action that determines the decision but whether the action itself is perceived to be right, is
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: ethical relativism

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: ethical egoism

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: utilitarianism

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Kantian ethics

explanation.solution_text_en: Kantian ethics is deontological or non-consequential: moral judgment focuses on whether the action and its guiding duty/principle are right, not only on the consequences produced.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Ethical Values

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following belongs to the area of micro-economics?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The analysis of inputs and exports

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: The behavior of consumers and producers

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The analysis of investment

choices.label: D

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is correct about traditional instruments of justice?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Traditional courts may not reflect the values and norms of society

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Traditional courts are not expected to function side by side with modern courts

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: In some cases, they may not be locally established by the people

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Traditional instruments of justice are vary from place to place

explanation.solution_text_en: Indigenous and traditional justice institutions are rooted in local customs, histories and social structures, so their forms and procedures vary from place to place.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 4: Indigenous Knowledge; Grade 10 - Unit 4: Peace and Indigenous Conflict Resolution

choices.text_en: the objectivity of the court

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: avoidance of discrimination

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: treatment of every person as individual

explanation.solution_text_en: Religious prejudice can undermine impartiality and equal treatment before the law. Courts should avoid discrimination and assess each person and case objectively.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 3: Good Governance; Unit 6: Human Rights

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is correct about the permanent tendency to lead one's life on outside support?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Dependency syndrome

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Dependency fatigue

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Relative dependency

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Donor fatigue

explanation.solution_text_en: Dependency syndrome refers to a persistent tendency to rely on outside support rather than developing the capacity to meet needs independently.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Problem-Solving Skills; Grade 10 - Unit 8: Global Issues

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following refers to a disposition that can be taken as the manifestation of a patriotic citizen?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Behaviors which disrespect or hurt others, such as lying and stealing

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Breaking rules and laws which govern the society

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Looking after the well-being of one's own self at the expense of others

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: An attitude of openness and respect for differences which exist among people

explanation.solution_text_en: Patriotism in a diverse society is compatible with openness, tolerance and respect for differences. Lying, stealing, breaking lawful rules and sacrificing others for selfish benefit contradict civic responsibility.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 6: National Unity through Diversity; Grade 10 - Unit 7: Patriotism

questions.question_text_en: The failure to be behave responsibly in the affairs of the society and the state will result in

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: strengthening the bond of trust

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: paving the way for dictatorship

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: greater responsibility in the future

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: enhancement of democracy

explanation.solution_text_en: When citizens and officials fail to act responsibly, accountability and trust can weaken, creating conditions in which arbitrary or authoritarian practices may grow. Responsible participation supports democracy rather than undermining it.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Units 1 and 3: Democracy; Good Governance

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is different concerning the new perspective of patriotism in Ethiopia?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Increasing productivity and fighting poverty

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Defending the country from enemies

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Inventing a new medicine or machine

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Respecting law of the country

explanation.solution_text_en: The newer civic understanding of patriotism extends beyond military defense to productive work, innovation, poverty reduction and respect for law. Defending the country from enemies is the more traditional security-centered example.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Patriotism

questions.question_text_en: Acting to promote the common good is a quality of patriots that requires
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: actions which frighten or force the government

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: commitment to support political objectives of a specific ethnic group

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: a commitment to perform one's own duty and take moral responsibility

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: consideration of the private prior to public interest

explanation.solution_text_en: Promoting the common good requires citizens to fulfill duties and accept moral responsibility for how their actions affect society. It is not the same as advancing a narrow group or private interest.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Patriotism; Grade 9 - Unit 1: Ethical Values

explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 Economics - Unit 6: Poverty and Inequality

questions.question_text_en: Among the following one can be classified as a group responsibility. Which one?

questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Traveling a long distance to and from school

choices.text_en: Making sure that the teaching-learning process works smoothly

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Obeying orders from teachers and other staff

explanation.solution_text_en: A group responsibility is a duty shared by members of a group. Keeping the teaching-learning process running smoothly requires cooperation among students, teachers and school staff.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Ethical Values and social responsibility; Grade 10 - Democracy and civic participation

questions.question_text_en: Ato Kassa is an engineer who believes that he has a responsibility to be honest and truthful in every course of his life. This responsibility of Ato Kassa arises from his
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: custom and tradition

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: law

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: occupation

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: moral principles

explanation.solution_text_en: Honesty and truthfulness are ethical duties grounded in moral principles, regardless of whether a specific law or workplace rule commands them in every situation.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Ethical Values

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is correct about the correlation between national and global security?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Terrorist attacks on western countries will not affect the economy of poor countries

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Fighting against terrorism at the national level is a contribution to the wellbeing of the global community

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: National security can be achieved fully in the absence of global security

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The prevalence of security in Ethiopia has a zero impact on the Middle East

explanation.solution_text_en: Security threats can cross borders, so national efforts against terrorism and violent extremism can contribute to regional and global security. Cooperation is therefore important while respecting law and human rights.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 8: Foreign Relations; Grade 10 - Global Issues

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following states correctly the major duty of patriotic citizens?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Using the state's secrets for political interest

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Fighting against the government and its policies

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Criticizing the government for political gain

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Playing an exemplary role in defending national security

explanation.solution_text_en: Patriotic citizenship includes lawful contribution to the security and sovereignty of the country. Using state secrets, political violence or criticism merely for personal gain does not express that duty.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Patriotism

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following can be considered the most important contribution of Ethiopia globally?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Poverty reduction

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Global warming

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Peace keeping

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Democratization process

explanation.solution_text_en: Ethiopia has a long record of participation in UN-authorized peacekeeping and peace-support operations. Peacekeeping is therefore the clearest internationally recognized contribution among the choices. Evidence check: UN Peacekeeping: Ethiopia - long record of Ethiopian participation in UN-authorized peace operations.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 History - Unit 8: Post-1991 Developments in Ethiopia; Grade 9 Citizenship - Foreign Relations

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is correct concerning ethical standards and the working environment?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: A smooth working environment can be maintained without ethical standards

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: A harmonious working environment requires respecting some ethical rules

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Ethical standards are the same in all professions and organizations

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The necessity of ethical standards is to keep the interest of the company

explanation.solution_text_en: Ethical standards such as honesty, fairness, respect and responsibility help build trust and cooperation in a workplace. A harmonious work environment therefore requires ethical rules and conduct.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Ethical Values

questions.question_text_en: Among the following one is the major principle of democracy. Which one?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Censorship of the press

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Free, fair and periodic election

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Lack of transparency and accountability

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Limited public participation

explanation.solution_text_en: Regular free and fair elections are a core democratic mechanism through which citizens choose representatives and hold political authority accountable.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Democracy and Democratization

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following summarizes the interdependence between human and democratic rights?
questions.review_note: The current curriculum emphasizes that human rights are universal, indivisible and interdependent. The one-direction wording in C is therefore an oversimplification; democratic and human rights mutually reinforce one another.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: There is no limitation attached to human right as well as democratic rights

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Human rights arise independent from democratic rights

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: It is the prevalence of democratic right that ensures human rights

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: It is the prevalence of human rights that guarantees democratic rights

explanation.solution_text_en: Human rights and democratic rights reinforce one another: democratic institutions help protect rights, while respect for human rights is also necessary for meaningful democracy. Among the options, C is the closest to this relationship.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Units 1 and 6: Democracy; Human Rights

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is different from the rest in terms of protecting the abuse of power?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The Check and Balance System

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The Human Rights Commission

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The office of Ombudsman

explanation.solution_text_en: The Human Rights Commission, Ombudsman and anti-corruption bodies are specialized accountability institutions. Checks and balances, by contrast, is a broader constitutional system of distributing and restraining public power, so it differs from the other three.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 3: Good Governance

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following explains the core value of Ethiopia's foreign relation?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Importing new technologies

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Developing cultural relations

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Attracting foreign investment

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Promoting the sovereignty of the country

explanation.solution_text_en: A central aim of foreign policy is protection of national sovereignty and national interest while pursuing peaceful cooperation and mutual benefit. The other choices are possible policy tools or outcomes rather than the core value. Evidence check: FDRE Constitution, Art. 86; current Grade 9 Citizenship Education, Unit 8.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 8: Ethiopia's Foreign Relations in East Africa; FDRE Constitution Art. 86

questions.question_text_en: What was the main reason for the ratification of the first written constitution of Ethiopia?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Protection and enforcement of rights and liberties of the people

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Promotion of the equality of nations, nationalities and peoples of Ethiopia

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Legalizing and strengthening the Emperor's absolute power

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Upholding socialist values and protecting territorial integrity

explanation.solution_text_en: The 1931 Constitution was Ethiopia's first written constitution and formalized a strongly centralized imperial order, strengthening the legal position and authority of Emperor Haile Selassie. Evidence check: Current Grade 12 History, Unit 3 - political developments in Ethiopia to 1941.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 History - Unit 3: Ethiopia, mid-19th century to 1941

questions.question_text_en: What is the ultimate purpose of the protection of the environment from any damage?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Generating income that would promote economic growth

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Enriching the topsoil and maintaining its fertility

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Replant trees and where they are sparse

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Decreasing health risks and improving the living standards of the people

explanation.solution_text_en: Environmental protection ultimately serves human and ecological well-being by reducing pollution and health risks and supporting sustainable living standards. Income, soil fertility and reforestation are important means or benefits, not the broadest ultimate purpose.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 Economics - Unit 8: Economy, Environment and Climate Change

questions.question_text_en: Which of the following is a major impact of sexism on the world of work?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Attaining of sustainable development

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Encouraging women to get involved in their jobs actively

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Empowering women on raising children

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Limiting the potential of women to benefit society

explanation.solution_text_en: Sexism restricts opportunities based on sex and can prevent women from fully using their skills and contributing to workplaces and society. This reduces both individual opportunity and social development.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 6: Human Rights

questions.question_text_en: What is the consequence of dependency on national development?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Scientific and technological advancement

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Development of democratic culture

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Economic growth and poverty reduction

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Economic and social disparity

explanation.solution_text_en: Long-term dependency can weaken self-reliance and productive capacity and may deepen social and economic inequality. The other choices describe positive development outcomes, not typical risks of dependency.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 8: Globalization and Global Issues; Grade 11 Economics - Development

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is true about the risks of dependency?
questions.review_note: This is a risk or critical perspective, not an inevitable outcome of every international economic relationship.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: It promotes environmental governance and sustainable development

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Wealthy nations can have multifaceted influence on poor nations

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Poor nations provide market access to wealthy nations

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Foreign-owned companies can use cheap labour

explanation.solution_text_en: A dependency risk is that economically powerful states or institutions may gain disproportionate influence over weaker economies. This is commonly discussed as a concern in dependency and globalization analysis.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 8: Globalization and Global Issues

questions.question_text_en: A traditional saving method where people living in a community contribute a fixed amount every month so that it would ease the cost of funeral ceremony in case a family member dies

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Iddir

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Bank

explanation.solution_text_en: Iddir is a community mutual-support association in which members make regular contributions, commonly to help families meet funeral-related costs and other emergencies.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 4: Indigenous Knowledge; Grade 11 Economics - Saving

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following describes the concept of civic participation?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Citizens' obligation to enhance social development and support

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: A voluntary cooperation and activity to promote the common good

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: An effort towards government reforms in order to attain political goal

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Any activity that has a political, religious and military activity

explanation.solution_text_en: Civic participation is voluntary involvement by citizens in activities that improve community life and promote the common good. It can be political or non-political.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Democracy and Democratization

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is correct regarding the ultimate purpose of reading?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Reading essentially benefits the writer than the reader

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Reading helps acquire new knowledge continuously and contributes to the well-being of society

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The objective of reading is only to acquire knowledge

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The main aim of reading is to spend one's time extravagantly

explanation.solution_text_en: Reading is a continuing way to acquire knowledge, develop understanding and contribute more effectively to personal and social well-being. It is not limited to a single narrow purpose.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Problem-Solving Skills and informed citizenship

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following alternatives is correct regarding the necessity of respect for work?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Respect for work shall be determined by the type of job that one does

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Any work should be respected if and only if it generates money to the individual

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Lack of respect for work tends to push people to see an easy way for getting money

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Every profession should be honoured for it benefits the doer

explanation.solution_text_en: Respect for work rejects the idea that only certain jobs deserve dignity. When people look down on productive work, they may be attracted to effortless or unethical ways of obtaining money.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Ethical Values

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following choices can best be classified as the negative impact of globalization on the Ethiopian economy?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Increased dependency on cheaper goods and services

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Close relationship with other countries

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Increased flow of goods and services

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Sharing of ideas and policies

explanation.solution_text_en: Globalization can increase access to trade, ideas and services, but excessive reliance on imported low-cost goods and services can weaken domestic capacity and create dependency.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 8: Globalization and Global Issues

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is a reflection of relying on others?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Not prepared to face the truth about oneself

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Being realistic and not excusing your weaknesses

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Not exaggerating one's weaknesses and looking down on one's own self confidently

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Not thinking one-self more than he/she should

explanation.solution_text_en: Over-reliance on others can discourage realistic self-assessment and the willingness to confront one's own limitations. The other options describe healthier, more balanced self-perception.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Problem-Solving Skills

questions.question_text_en: What will happen if one fails to discharge his/her own constitutional obligation?

questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: It will enable the government to be more accountable and transparent

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: It will limit the power of the government and prevents its abuse of power

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: A democratic culture shall flourish in the society

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: One's constitutional rights shall be compromised

explanation.solution_text_en: The item intends to connect rights with responsibilities: failure to meet civic obligations can have lawful consequences and can undermine the conditions in which rights are protected. D is the closest option to that intended lesson.
