questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is an area in which both the federal and regional governments exercise concurrent power in the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: National defense and security

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Financial policy matters

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Revenue and tax collection

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Conducting foreign policy matters

explanation.solution_text_en: The FDRE Constitution identifies areas of concurrent taxation in which federal and state governments jointly levy and collect specified taxes. Revenue and tax collection is therefore the option that reflects concurrent authority. Evidence check: FDRE Constitution, Art. 98 - concurrent federal/state taxation (Refworld).
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 5: Federalism in Ethiopia; FDRE Constitution Art. 98

questions.question_text_en: What is the main aim of promoting political tolerance in a democratic system of governance?
questions.review_note: Tolerance does not require eliminating or homogenizing differences. The intended idea is peaceful unity/coexistence across differences.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: To unify differences among ethnic, religious and political groups

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: To check the abuse of power in governments

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: To enforce the government to conduct its affairs in a transparent way

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: To hold public officials accountable for any failure in official duties

explanation.solution_text_en: Political tolerance enables people with different political, ethnic and religious views to coexist peacefully and participate without suppressing one another. A is closest if “unify differences” is understood as building unity across diversity, not erasing differences.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 6: National Unity through Diversity; Grade 10 - Unit 1: Democracy

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following explains best the democratic notion of keeping the balance between rights and duties of citizens?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Failure to respect constitutional obligation is punishable by law

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Not to perform constitutional duty implies not use constitutional right

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The use of every right requires an obligation to be fulfilled

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The idea of equal number of constitutional rights and duties

explanation.solution_text_en: The exercise of rights takes place alongside duties to respect the rights of others and the lawful constitutional order. Rights and duties are related, but they are not required to exist in equal numerical amounts.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 6: Human Rights; Unit 7: Patriotism

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following describes best the characteristics of an unlimited form of government?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Prevalence of basic rights and freedoms

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Utter power and ignorance of the rule of law

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Absence of arbitrary power

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Power emanates from the people

explanation.solution_text_en: Unlimited government is characterized by concentrated or arbitrary power and weak effective limits from law and institutions. That is the opposite of constitutional rule, protected rights and popular sovereignty.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 3: Constitution and Constitutionalism; Grade 10 - Good Governance

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is correct regarding an individual responsibility?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: A farmer and a factory worker can have the same personal responsibilities

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Personal responsibility does not involve a balance between your personal and social interests

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Individual responsibilities do not vary from person to person

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Different occupations determine the type and extent of personal responsibility

explanation.solution_text_en: Some personal responsibilities are shaped by a person's role, occupation and circumstances. A farmer, factory worker, public official and student may therefore have different role-specific duties in addition to shared civic duties.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Ethical Values

questions.question_text_en: An economic system in which individuals decide what to produce and how it is distributed in line with priorities set by the government
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Mixed Economic System

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Planned Economic System

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Command Economic System

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Free Market Economic System

explanation.solution_text_en: A mixed economic system combines private market decisions with government regulation, public provision and policy priorities. Neither the market nor the state alone determines all production and distribution.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 11 Economics - Economic Systems; Grade 12 Economics - Macroeconomic Policy

questions.question_text_en: Woizero Almaz is personnel in one of the land administration offices of Addis Ababa city administration. She usually spends too much time talking to her friends over tea and coffee while her office is loaded with customers. Such an attitude of the personnel violates an ethical principle of
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: loyalty

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: honesty

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: punctuality

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: willingness to learn

explanation.solution_text_en: Spending excessive work time on private conversations while customers wait violates punctuality and responsible use of working time.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Ethical Values

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following explains the impact of dependency?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: It can cause a loss of political will and encourage belief on outside help

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: It nurtures one's ability to support and take care of his/her-self

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: It enables oneself to make decisions free from influence and control of others

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: It develops one's self confidence in taking initiatives and benefit society

explanation.solution_text_en: Dependency can weaken initiative and political will by encouraging repeated reliance on outside help. The other choices describe qualities of self-reliance rather than dependency.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Problem-Solving Skills; Grade 10 - Global Issues

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following demonstrates the best way to combat the habit of dependency?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Prohibiting any act of begging which needs the help of others

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: To enable citizens develop self-reliance through understanding their good qualities

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Totally cutting off the food aid that rich countries give to poor countries

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Training citizens how great and perfect they are

explanation.solution_text_en: Dependency is best addressed by building realistic self-knowledge, confidence, skills and capacity for self-reliance. Total rejection of all assistance or exaggerated self-praise is not a sound solution.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Problem-Solving Skills

questions.question_text_en: What are the criteria that can qualify a government as having a legitimate power and authority?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Existence of rule of men than rule of law

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Having the power to rule which lacks moral authority

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Receiving its mandate to govern from the people

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Having constitution, but not constitutional rule

explanation.solution_text_en: In a democratic system, legitimate political authority rests on the consent and mandate of the people, exercised through constitutional institutions and lawful elections.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Democracy and Democratization

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following listed alternatives states the exclusive power of the central government in federal Ethiopia?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: To have their own constitutions together with FDRE constitution

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: To conduct foreign relations and recruit armed forces

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Recruiting and managing their own police force

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: To create enabling conditions for investment

explanation.solution_text_en: The FDRE Constitution assigns foreign relations and national defense/armed forces to the federal government. State governments have their own constitutionally assigned powers, including state police and administration. Evidence check: FDRE Constitution, Art. 51 - federal powers including foreign affairs and national defense (Refworld).
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 5: Federalism in Ethiopia; FDRE Constitution Art. 51

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following statements is correct about Ethiopian foreign relation?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: It is based on coexistence and cooperation states and people

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Its core value is dominating the region and redefining the order

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: It is consistent or not geographically determined with some countries

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: A change in government will not affect the foreign relation and policy

explanation.solution_text_en: Current citizenship education presents Ethiopia's foreign relations in terms of sovereignty, peaceful coexistence, cooperation, equality and mutual benefit. A is the option that best reflects those principles. Evidence check: FDRE Constitution, Art. 86 - principles of external relations; current Grade 9 Citizenship, Unit 8.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 8: Ethiopia's Foreign Relations in East Africa; FDRE Constitution Art. 86

questions.question_text_en: A conflict resolution mechanism through formally established procedural rules, customs or practices which involves a process of carrying on a suit before the law is called
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: negotiation

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: mediation

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: litigation

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: arbitration

explanation.solution_text_en: Litigation is the formal resolution of a dispute through established court procedures and a legal suit. Negotiation, mediation and arbitration are alternative dispute-resolution mechanisms.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 4: Peace and Indigenous Conflict Resolution

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following choices can be classified as an instance of the curative approach employed in the fight against corruption?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Laws and rules related to financial administration

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Bringing the corrupt officials to justice

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Registration of property

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Ethical Regulation

explanation.solution_text_en: A curative anti-corruption measure responds after wrongdoing by investigating, prosecuting and bringing offenders to justice. Financial rules, asset registration and ethics codes are mainly preventive measures.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 3: Good Governance

questions.question_text_en: Among the following, one is the role of institutions than individuals regarding the fight against corruption and abuse of power. Which one?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Making activities transparent and holding officials accountable for any fault

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Respecting the religious and customary values

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Exposing corrupt people and turn away from any corrupt practices

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Being honest and truthful in day-to-day activities

explanation.solution_text_en: Institutions combat corruption by establishing transparent processes, oversight and mechanisms that hold officials accountable. The other options describe mainly personal ethical conduct.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 3: Good Governance

questions.question_text_en: In countries where there is no rule of law,
questions.review_note: The wording “order shall break out” is grammatically defective; the intended meaning is that political and social order may break down.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: people are prohibited from violating the rights of others

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: those who govern shall exercise limited power

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: basic rights of individuals and groups will be respected

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: political and social order shall break out

explanation.solution_text_en: Where rule of law is absent, arbitrary power and rights violations can produce political and social disorder. A functioning rule of law instead limits government and protects rights.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 3: Good Governance

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is correct concerning the equality of Nations, Nationalities and Peoples of Ethiopia?
questions.review_note: C is also broadly true because the Constitution guarantees equality and rights. D is chosen because it states a specific constitutional mechanism connected to equal political participation, making this item partly ambiguous.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: It does not involve a restorative justice to repair damages done in the past

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: The federal structure of government limited the equality of the people

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The constitution guaranteed equal protection and the rights given to the people

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The right to self-government is an ingredient for insuring equal political participation

explanation.solution_text_en: The Constitution links equality of Nations, Nationalities and Peoples with rights of self-government and equitable representation. Those arrangements are intended to support equal political participation within the federal system. Evidence check: FDRE Constitution, Art. 39(3) - self-government and equitable representation.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 5: Federalism in Ethiopia; FDRE Constitution Art. 39(3)

questions.question_text_en: Among the following one is different with regard to the relationship between individual and public interests. Which one?
questions.review_note: The current curriculum does not teach that public interest automatically overrides individual rights. Any limitation on rights must have a lawful and constitutionally justified basis; C is only the closest available formulation.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Individual rights should always precede the public interest

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Both individual and public interests should always be equally promoted in every action of a government

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Personal interests are protected only to the extent that they do not affect the public

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Individual interests might not be given up even to promote the benefit of the society

explanation.solution_text_en: A democratic constitutional order seeks to protect personal rights while also permitting lawful measures for legitimate public interests. C is the closest option because it recognizes that individual interests are not absolute when they harm the public.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Units 6-7: Human Rights; Patriotism

questions.question_text_en: Ato Kinde is a resident in Addis Ababa who is engaged in a retail business sector. He complained to the Wereda Income and Revenue Authority that he is requested to pay more amount of tax than those who have the same amount of earning with him. Accordingly, which principle of taxation is violated by the Wereda Income and Revenue Authority in this case?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Tax avoidance

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Vertical Equity

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Ability to pay

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Horizontal equity

explanation.solution_text_en: Horizontal equity means taxpayers with similar ability to pay or similar income should bear similar tax burdens. Charging Ato Kinde more than others with the same earning violates this principle.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 12 Economics - Unit 5: Tax Theory and Practice

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is the negative impact of international monetary organizations on the development of third world countries?
questions.review_note: This should not be read as the official purpose of the IMF or World Bank. Their stated mandates concern macroeconomic/financial stability (IMF) and long-term development/poverty reduction (World Bank). A represents a critical perspective on possible influence, not their formal goal.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Influencing a country politically and culturally

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Financing the development efforts of a country

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Stimulating the economy to produce more

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Making funds available for investment

explanation.solution_text_en: Among the options, A is the only stated negative effect and reflects a critical dependency/globalization perspective: external finance can be accompanied by political or policy influence. The other options describe possible financing or development benefits. Evidence check: IMF official factsheet distinguishes formal IMF and World Bank mandates; A is treated only as a critical dependency perspective.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 8: Globalization and Global Issues; Grade 11 Economics - Development

questions.question_text_en: Among the following one is correct concerning the main goal of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank. Which one?
questions.review_note: D simplifies two distinct institutional mandates. It should not be treated as a complete definition of either institution.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Mobilization of capital in the local area

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Liberalization of economies for Western products

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: They working mainly in response to what happens in the economy

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Increasing production and employment rate

explanation.solution_text_en: The IMF and World Bank share a broad objective of improving living standards: the IMF focuses on macroeconomic and financial stability, while the World Bank focuses on long-term development and poverty reduction. D is the closest available outcome among the choices. Evidence check: IMF official factsheet: IMF focuses on macroeconomic/financial stability; World Bank on long-term development and poverty reduction.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 11 Economics - Trade, Finance and Development; Grade 12 Economics - Macroeconomic Policy and Poverty

secondary_curriculum_links: Grade 12 Economics - Macroeconomic Policy and Poverty

questions.question_text_en: An individual who is charismatic, attractive, appealing, charming and influential is said to possess the personal quality of a leader, which is
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: engaging

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: versatile

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: a motivator

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: realistic

explanation.solution_text_en: “Engaging” describes a person whose manner is attractive, appealing and able to hold the attention or interest of others.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Ethical and interpersonal qualities

questions.question_text_en: Freedom of the press is vital to enhance the public participation and public responsibility for the reason that
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: citizens can write whatever pleases them

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: it obliges the government to have a limited power

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: it is an information channel between the government and the people

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: it serves as citizen's instrument of opposition

explanation.solution_text_en: A free press can transmit information between citizens and government, support informed public debate and expose matters of public concern. This strengthens participation and accountability.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Units 1 and 3: Democracy; Good Governance

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following is correct about the concept of judicial review?
questions.review_note: Ethiopia has a distinct constitutional-interpretation system. Under FDRE Constitution Arts. 83-84, constitutional disputes are finally decided by the House of the Federation after consideration by the Council of Constitutional Inquiry. Therefore D is a general definition, not a complete description of Ethiopia's institutional arrangement.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Judicial review is limited to declaring laws and decisions unlawful

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: In Ethiopia federal supreme court the only responsible organ to declare a given law or action unconstitutional

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: It is a courts power to review the ministerial office of the government but not to review legislative and executive branch of government

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: It is a courts power to invalidate legislative and executive actions as being unconstitutional

explanation.solution_text_en: In general constitutional theory, judicial review is the power of courts to assess government acts and invalidate legislative or executive action that conflicts with a constitution. That is the definition stated in D. Evidence check: FDRE Constitution, Arts. 83-84 - House of the Federation and Council of Constitutional Inquiry roles.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 3: Constitution and Constitutionalism; Grade 10 - Good Governance

questions.question_text_en: The overall purpose of learning to plan and to save time is to develop the habit of
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: paying back what one owes to others

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: saving for spending excessive amount of money on funerals

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: living within the limits of your capacity

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: saving to buy extravagant items

explanation.solution_text_en: Planning and saving time develop self-discipline and the habit of living and acting within one's available resources and capacity rather than wasting them.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Ethical Values and problem-solving skills

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following can be classified as an extravagant practice?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Equb, a traditional way of saving to fulfill one's future dreams

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Tezkar, a large expenditure on funeral ceremony after a person passes away

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Iddir, a traditional saving for funeral purposes

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: A simple wedding ceremony which costs a small amount of money

explanation.solution_text_en: Tezkar can involve very large funeral-related expenditure and is therefore the extravagant practice among these choices. Equb and Iddir are commonly used as saving or mutual-support arrangements.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 4: Indigenous Knowledge; Grade 11 Economics - Saving

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following can be distinguished best as a political participation?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Taking part in voting

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Joining the struggle against drug abuse

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Involvement in the fight against corruption

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Active participation to combat the spread of HIV/AIDS

explanation.solution_text_en: Voting is a direct form of political participation because citizens take part in choosing representatives or deciding public questions through elections.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Democracy and Democratization

questions.question_text_en: What are the main distinguishing features of wisdom in contrast to knowledge?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: It does not involve questioning what exists around us

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: It is not a life-time process

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: It is handling acquired knowledge for good use

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: It is not acquired, rather inborn

explanation.solution_text_en: Wisdom is the sound application of knowledge to good and sensible purposes. It involves judgment rather than mere possession of information.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 7: Problem-Solving Skills

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following explains the virtue of truthfulness in contrast with falsehood?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Truthfulness and honesty are mutually exclusive

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: Social norms and religions are expected to uphold truthfulness

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: Knowledge serves as a tool of falsehood rather than truthfulness

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Truthfulness should be upheld to gain respect from others

explanation.solution_text_en: Truthfulness is supported by ethical norms and, in many communities, by religious and social values. It should be practiced as a moral virtue, not merely as a tactic to gain respect.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Ethical Values

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following explains the right to privacy of human rights?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The right to the free development of one's own personality

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: The right to respect for human dignity, reputation and honor

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The right not to be deprived of one's life

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The right not to be subjected to searches of one's personal property

explanation.solution_text_en: The right to privacy protects people against arbitrary or unlawful interference with their home, correspondence and personal sphere, including improper searches. D is the option that most directly describes that protection. Evidence check: FDRE Constitution, Art. 26 - right to privacy.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 6: Human Rights; FDRE Constitution Art. 26

questions.question_text_en: Among the following one can be classified as a human right abuse than democratic one in Ethiopia. Which one?
questions.review_note: The item is not cleanly single-answer. Hazardous child labour (A), discriminatory inheritance (B) and unlawful seizure of property (D) can also violate human rights. C is selected as the clearest direct prohibition of cruel/inhuman treatment.
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: Forcing children to perform work in hazardous or harmful to their health

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: The denial of women to enjoy equal treatment in the inheritance of property

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The cruel and inhuman treatment of children in schools and other institutions

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The seizure of one's own property which is under his/her personal possession

explanation.solution_text_en: Cruel or inhuman treatment is a core violation of personal integrity and human dignity, so C is the clearest human-rights-abuse example in the list. Evidence check: FDRE Constitution, Arts. 18 and 36 - protection from cruel treatment and rights of children.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 6: Human Rights; FDRE Constitution Arts. 18 and 36

questions.question_text_en: All are distinctive features of Ethiopian society after the establishment of the democratic system except one. Which one?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The provision of all cultural groups' equal opportunities for their development

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: The treatment of some cultures superior over others

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The equality of Nations, Nationalities and Peoples of Ethiopia

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The right to promote and develop one's cultural identity

explanation.solution_text_en: A democratic multicultural order is based on equal dignity and opportunity for cultural groups and protection of cultural identity. Treating some cultures as inherently superior contradicts those principles.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 9 Citizenship Education - Units 5-6: Multiculturalism; National Unity through Diversity

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following organs of the federal government of Ethiopia mainly involved in the enforcement of the various policies and strategies designed for administering the country?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The Parliament

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: The Legislative branch

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The Executive Branch

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: The Judiciary branch

explanation.solution_text_en: The executive branch is responsible for carrying out and administering laws, policies and government strategies. The legislature makes laws and oversees government; the judiciary resolves legal disputes.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 3: Good Governance; Unit 5: Federalism

questions.question_text_en: Which one of the following fact clearly shows the characteristics of indirect democracy as a form of government?
questions.source_name: EUEE Civics and Ethical Education Hamlie 2015 E.C. Booklet 653

choices.label: A
choices.text_en: The representative of the people are openly appointed by the chief executive body

choices.label: B
choices.text_en: The majority of the people are required to withdraw from the decision making activities of the government

choices.label: C
choices.text_en: The government authorities have unlimited political power to safeguard their own interest

choices.label: D
choices.text_en: Any political decision of the people is made through their elected representative

explanation.solution_text_en: In indirect or representative democracy, citizens exercise political authority mainly through representatives they elect to make public decisions on their behalf.
explanation.key_concept: Grade 10 Citizenship Education - Unit 1: Democracy and Democratization
